stored.fact: Kira Studio is a native macOS workbench combining a visual database client for ten engines with an HTTP/gRPC API client.
Kira Studio is built on Wails (Go) and Vue 3.
Kira Studio switches between Studio (database), Api, Automations and Docker modes with one button.
The repository contains a sibling app, Kira Space: a native git client and code workspace with coding agents, memory store, terminal and phone view.
The Kira Space README is at apps/kira-space/README.md.
Kira Studio is beta.
Kira Studio supports only macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon (arm64), and only dark mode.
Kira Studio builds are ad-hoc signed and not notarized.
Each new Kira Studio build counts as a different app to the Keychain, so first launch after an update may prompt for access; choose Always Allow.
Kira Studio saved credentials are encrypted at rest in the macOS Keychain.
scripts/install.sh, with --app=studio or --app=space, downloads the latest release disk image and installs the app into /Applications.
Installing with scripts/install.sh avoids the Gatekeeper prompt, unlike a DMG downloaded through a browser.
The installed app checks GitHub for a newer release and offers to update.
Nothing installs until the user clicks Update; silent auto-update is deliberately absent.
Building Kira Studio from source uses bun run package:studio, which first installs the Bun workspace, Go module and pinned wails3 CLI.
bun run package:studio outputs apps/kira-studio/bin/Kira Studio.app and Kira Studio.dmg.

stored.fact: Kira Studio supports PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL (8.0.16+), SQLite, ClickHouse, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka, SQS and S3.
In Kira Studio, ClickHouse supports insert only.
In Kira Studio, Redis writes are for string keys, with delete on any type.
In Kira Studio, Kafka supports produce only.
In Kira Studio, SQS supports send and delete.
In Kira Studio, Stop cancels the operation itself (pg_cancel_backend, KILL QUERY, cursor abort, consumer stop), not only its display.
SQS never polls on its own in Kira Studio; reads happen only when the user presses Poll.
ReceiveMessage hides messages from real consumers, which is why Kira Studio does not poll SQS automatically.
Each Kira Studio connection has a read-only guard enforced in the backend.
Each Kira Studio connection can have an optional pre-connect script, for example a port-forward.
In Kira Studio, Update credentials on a saved connection changes only its username and password.
Kira Studio session restore reopens tabs without auto-connecting.
Kira Studio stages SQL edits as a pending change set with an exact command preview; nothing reaches the database until commit.
Kira Studio document, key/value and stream writes apply immediately.
Kira Studio foreign-key navigation works for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.
Kira Studio column masking (PII) offers six masks.
Kira Studio column masking is display-only; the data itself is never changed.
Kira Studio uses three-tier caching with no speculative prefetch.
Kira Studio caching is documented in docs/PERF.md.
Revealing a saved password in Kira Studio requires Touch ID or system password confirmation.
A Kira Studio Automations smart script is a prompt run by headless Claude Code, not a shell command.
A smart script has typed parameters, a model, a budget, a timeout and a list of permitted tools and MCP servers.
Recurring Kira Studio automation scripts use a cron schedule.
A due automation run asks for confirmation by default and never replays a missed run.
Kira Studio Docker mode manages the local engine or a saved context.
A remote tcp:// Docker engine without TLS works but is flagged as insecure in the Kira Studio UI.
Incognito tabs in the Kira Studio Api client are a per-tab toggle.
Nothing from an incognito tab is saved: no history, no log, no variable writes.
The Kira Studio Api client keeps the last 30 responses per request in its response history.
Kira Studio Api client gRPC calls, unary and streaming, share collections, environments and variables with HTTP.
The Kira Studio Database MCP server is optional and off by default.
Database MCP is enabled from Settings → Database MCP.
The Kira Studio Database MCP server listens on loopback only, on port 8766.
The Database MCP server uses its own bearer token.
The Kira Studio Database MCP server exposes six tools: list_connections, list_children, describe_table, describe_schema, run_query, explain_query.
Database MCP is deny by default: a connection stays invisible to the AI client until the user exposes it.
Database MCP per-connection read, write and DDL permissions are each allow, deny or prompt.
Database MCP permission defaults are read allow, write prompt, DDL deny.
Prompt mode waits for approval of the exact statement; a statement that can't be classified gets the strictest mode.
With auto-explain on, queries estimated above the expensive-query threshold pause for approval in Database MCP.
PII masking rules apply to Database MCP results before the AI client sees them.
Building Kira Studio from source requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon (arm64) with Xcode command-line tools.
Building Kira Studio from source also requires Go 1.27+ and the Wails v3 CLI.
Kira Studio uses Bun as package manager, script runner and test runner.
Bun is build tooling only; nothing in Kira Studio ships a Node runtime.
Never run the bun run screenshots script beside a UI test run, because it rebuilds frontend/dist.
The bun run screenshots output is byte-identical across runs.
bun install installs Git hooks; pre-commit runs lint and typecheck.
The pre-push Git hook runs the Go build and linters.
Kira Studio stores its data in ~/.kira-studio/, overridable with KIRA_HOME.
Kira Studio is a single native Go process (Wails v3) handling windowing, IPC, SQLite storage and all database drivers in-process.
